section_summary: This section contains duplicate and signed original copies of Embassy Tokyo's Despatch No. 419 transmitting Report No. 80 on political and economic conditions in Japan during May 1933, as well as Division of Far Eastern Affairs memoranda reviewing the May and June 1933 reports. Primary international subjects include Viscount Ishii's preliminary diplomatic mission to Washington ahead of the London Economic Conference, Japanese army operations in North China culminating in an armistice, and Soviet-Japanese negotiations over the sale of the Chinese Eastern Railway. Domestically, the materials cover Finance Minister Takahashi's decision to remain in office, the official report on the May 15, 1932 assassination of Premier Inukai, anti-British trade disputes affecting the cotton industry, and the academic freedom controversy involving Professor Takikawa at Kyoto Imperial University.

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Embassy Tokyo's monthly report on political and economic conditions in Japan for May 1933, transmitting Report No. 80 with annexes and a summary sheet.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: This document provides a detailed assessment of Japan's foreign affairs, internal politics, and economic conditions during May 1933. Diplomatic developments include Viscount Ishii and Eigo Fukai's departure for economic discussions in Washington and London, Japan's reaction to President Roosevelt's disarmament appeal, the Kwantung Army's push toward Peiping leading to a truce, and Soviet proposals to sell the Chinese Eastern Railway. Domestically, Finance Minister Takahashi's refusal to resign preserves the Saito cabinet against Seiyukai ambitions, while the government releases its investigative findings on the May 15 Incident implicating junior military officers and civilian radicals. Additional sections detail agrarian distress, plans for statutory oil control, discrimination against American businesses in Japan, and widespread protests surrounding the dismissal of Professor Takikawa at Kyoto Imperial University.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 419: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of May, 1933 (Report No. 80) [Duplicate Copy]

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing and analyzing key political and budgetary developments from Tokyo's May 1933 monthly report.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Salisbury reviews the political significance of Finance Minister Takahashi's decision to remain in office, explaining that it disappointed the Seiyukai's hopes of forming a one-party cabinet and was encouraged by the Genro and the military leadership. He highlights reported reconciliations between War Minister Araki and General Ugaki (Governor General of Chosen), noting that the Army's authority appears firmer than ever and that a return to party government is increasingly unlikely. The memorandum also notes Takahashi's statement to the press that national expenditures for fiscal year 1934 cannot be reduced, making higher taxation unavoidable.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo's Monthly Report for May 1933
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Signed original of Despatch No. 419 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmitting the Embassy's comprehensive monthly report on conditions in Japan for May 1933, complete with summary sheet and index.
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador to Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits the full signed original report on political, economic, and social developments in Japan for May 1933. The report examines Japanese policy at Washington and London, reception of President Roosevelt's disarmament appeal, hostilities in North China, the diplomatic controversy and sale negotiations regarding the Chinese Eastern Railway, and personnel shifts in the Foreign Office including Shigemitsu's appointment as Vice Minister. Domestically, it details the stabilization of the Saito cabinet following Takahashi's refusal to resign, the legal disposition of conspirators in the May 15 assassination of Premier Inukai, agricultural relief legislation, and protests over the forced ouster of Professor Takikawa from Kyoto Imperial University.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 419: Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of May, 1933 (Report No. 80) [Signed Original]

subfiles.about: Internal State Department memorandum summarizing and commenting on sections of Tokyo's monthly report for June 1933.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: This memorandum analyzes sections of Tokyo's monthly report for June 1933, noting rising anti-American press sentiment over the RFC's $50,000,000 credit to China and U.S. naval construction. It summarizes Japanese reactions to the London Economic Conference, preparations for Anglo-Japanese tariff negotiations at Simla headed by Setsuzo Sawada, and trade talks in London led by Chokiuro Kadono. In addition, it reviews ongoing Soviet-Japanese negotiations concerning the Chinese Eastern Railway and the opening of a conference at Hsinking regarding the abolition of extraterritoriality in Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo's Monthly Report for June 1933
subfiles.to: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
